events.description: Ittehad al-Mujahideen Pakistan suicide attack on a police compound mosque in northwestern Pakistan, becoming a gun battle with police
TTP assault on a checkpoint followed by car bomb on first responders
Three rounds of Pakistani airstrikes in eastern and southern Afghanistan; Pakistan claims terrorist hideouts hit, Taliban says only civilians
Attack in Faizabad, Badakhshan kills mid-level Taliban member; claimed by both NRF and Islamic State
US raid in Barmal district kills a top al-Qaeda Shura member at an al-Qaeda encampment; intelligence reveals Shorabak camp
US strike kills Zawahiri in Kabul with no blowback on the Taliban
First year of US war: 6,500 airstrikes, 17,500 munitions on Taliban targets
US withdrawal; Taliban seize American weapons systems

key_claims: Five years after the withdrawal the Taliban controls every district and all ministries, is recognized by China and Russia, and is morphing into the state; the 'moderate Haqqani faction vs Akhundzada' narrative is a trope that won't die.
Pakistan's good-Taliban/bad-Taliban policy has backfired: Hafiz Gul Bahadur, long a conduit for Pakistani support into Afghanistan, has turned on the state as part of Ittehad al-Mujahideen Pakistan.
The Taliban's victory made the Pakistani Taliban hungrier, not quieter; the TTP declared an Islamic Emirate of Pakistan.
The Taliban accepts Pakistani airstrikes as the price of hosting TTP/IMP/al-Qaeda auxiliaries; Pakistan should know the limits of air power from 20 years of US strikes.
Al-Qaeda operates under Taliban protection at little cost, as shown by the lack of blowback after the Zawahiri strike in Kabul.
ISKP and the NRF persist in the northeast (Faizabad attack) but are not a major threat to Taliban rule.
India is the only beneficiary of Pakistan-Taliban fighting.
